:::{#exm-minimum-description-length}
#### The minimum description length model for coin flips

<!-- no-figure: the example is one chosen model -->

The code below applies @def-minimum-description-length
to the lengths of @exm-two-part-description-length.
It prints the model with the smallest two-part description length,
and it prints the length of writing the $100$ flips out as plain heads and tails.

```{r}
#| label: minimum-description-length
chosen <- which.min(total_bits)
success_prob[chosen]
total_bits[chosen]
n_flips
```

The principle chooses the model with the probability of heads $`r success_prob[chosen]`$,
with a description of $`r round(total_bits[chosen], 1)`$ bits.
That is shorter than the $`r n_flips`$ bits of the flips themselves,
because the flips are far from fair.

:::
